knowledge_records.topic: Immediate actions after a road accident
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: After a road accident, the first priority is personal and scene safety before attempting to assist casualties. A bystander or involved person must stop safely, assess the scene for active hazards (moving traffic, fire, fuel leaks, electrical wires), ensure self-protection, check for casualties, and immediately contact emergency services (112) when injuries or scene hazards are present.
safe_actions: Stop only where it is safe to do so and avoid creating another collision risk.
Check for immediate hazards such as moving traffic, fire, smoke, fuel smell, broken glass, unstable vehicles, or damaged electrical systems.
Move yourself and uninjured people away from live traffic if it can be done safely.
Check whether anyone is injured, unconscious, trapped, bleeding heavily, or having difficulty breathing.
Call emergency services (112) immediately if anyone is injured or the scene is unsafe.
Stay calm and give clear location and hazard information to responders.
unsafe_actions: Do not rush into moving traffic to reach the accident scene.
Do not stand in a live traffic lane.
Do not ignore fire, smoke, fuel smell, or electrical hazards.
Do not attempt risky rescue actions beyond your physical ability or training.
escalation_criteria: Any visible injury
Unconscious person
Heavy bleeding
Person trapped in a vehicle
Fire, smoke, fuel leakage, or strong fuel smell
Vehicle blocking fast-moving traffic
Accident at night or in poor visibility
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by MoRTH Motor Vehicle Rules, ERSS 112 Guidelines, and Indian Red Cross First Aid Manual.

knowledge_records.topic: Preventing secondary collisions after a crash
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Secondary collisions pose a severe threat to crash survivors and bystanders. MoRTH and NHAI safety guidelines mandate switching on hazard warning lights immediately, positioning individuals off the carriageway, moving drivable vehicles off live lanes when safe, and using reflective warning triangles positioned safely behind the vehicle on high-speed corridors.
safe_actions: Switch on hazard warning lights immediately if the vehicle can be accessed safely.
Move mobile and uninjured people away from traffic and behind roadside crash barriers or shoulder areas.
If the vehicle is drivable and moving it is safe, move it off live traffic lanes to the hard shoulder.
If the vehicle cannot be moved safely, keep all people off the road and call emergency or highway patrol assistance.
Place warning devices or triangles behind the vehicle only if doing so does not expose you to oncoming traffic.
unsafe_actions: Do not stand directly behind or beside a damaged vehicle stopped on the carriageway.
Do not walk into fast-moving traffic lanes to place warning triangles.
Do not push or move a vehicle manually in a live lane when traffic speed makes it unsafe.
Do not remain in a dangerous traffic position to inspect vehicle damage or argue with other drivers.
escalation_criteria: Vehicle remains stuck in a live traffic lane
Fast-moving traffic is approaching the crash scene with limited stopping distance
Crash occurs on a highway, expressway, flyover, bridge, tunnel, or blind curve
Visibility is severely reduced due to darkness, rain, fog, dust, or smoke
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by MoRTH Rules of the Road Regulations and NHAI Highway Incident Management Protocols.

knowledge_records.topic: Approaching and protecting injured people after a crash
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: When helping injured crash victims, bystanders must avoid causing further physical trauma. According to Indian Red Cross and WHO trauma protocols, bystanders should approach only when the scene is safe, reassure the casualty, keep them calm, prevent unnecessary physical movement, and await professional medical responders unless an immediate life-threatening hazard (like fire) requires emergency evacuation.
safe_actions: Approach injured casualties only when you can do so safely without entering dangerous traffic or hazards.
Speak calmly, identify yourself, and reassure the injured person.
Instruct conscious casualties to stay still and avoid moving their head, neck, or limbs.
Keep the casualty warm and protected from traffic exposure while waiting for an ambulance.
Call emergency medical services (112 or 108) immediately for any unconsciousness, heavy bleeding, chest trauma, or severe pain.
unsafe_actions: Do not drag, pull, or lift an injured person unless there is an immediate life threat like fire, explosion risk, or oncoming traffic.
Do not twist, bend, or pull the neck or spine of a casualty with suspected spinal trauma.
Do not give food, water, tea, alcohol, or oral medication to a seriously injured person.
Do not remove a motorcycle helmet from an injured rider unless the airway is obstructed and you are trained in safe helmet removal.
escalation_criteria: Unconsciousness or decreased level of consciousness
Confusion, memory loss, or drowsiness after head impact
Suspected neck, spine, or pelvic injury
Heavy external bleeding or signs of internal shock
Difficulty breathing or noisy breathing
Casualty trapped inside crushed vehicle metal
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by Indian Red Cross Society First Aid Manual and WHO Basic Emergency Care protocols.

knowledge_records.topic: Severe bleeding after a road accident
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Massive external hemorrhage is a leading cause of preventable death in road crashes. Official Indian Red Cross first aid guidelines dictate applying firm, direct pressure on the wound using a clean cloth, pad, or dressing, maintaining continuous elevation if appropriate, keeping the casualty lying down, and securing immediate medical escalation.
safe_actions: Call emergency medical services (112 or 108) immediately for heavy bleeding.
Wear clean gloves or use a plastic barrier if available to avoid direct blood contact.
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure over the bleeding site with a clean cloth, sterile pad, or clothing.
Keep firm pressure applied continuously until medical responders take over.
Keep the injured casualty lying down and quiet to reduce shock.
unsafe_actions: Do not remove dressings that have soaked through; apply additional pads directly on top.
Do not remove deeply embedded glass, metal, or foreign objects from a wound; press around the object instead.
Do not apply unverified home remedies, cow dung, ashes, powders, or chemicals to open wounds.
Do not move a heavily bleeding casualty unnecessarily.
escalation_criteria: Bleeding is rapid, spurting, or does not stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure
Blood is pooling rapidly on the ground
Casualty becomes pale, cold, clammy, confused, or loses consciousness (signs of shock)
Traumatic amputation or crushed limb
Heavy bleeding accompanied by abdominal or chest wounds
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by Indian Red Cross Society First Aid Manual and MoHFW National Health Portal Guidelines.

knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Head, neck, and spinal trauma are frequent in high-impact vehicular collisions. Standard Red Cross and medical protocols mandate assuming spinal injury in any violent collision or unconscious crash victim. Bystanders must keep the head and neck in neutral alignment without traction, avoid turning the head, monitor breathing, and await specialized ambulance transport.
safe_actions: Call emergency medical help (112 / 108) immediately for any unconscious crash victim.
Assess breathing from a safe distance by watching for chest movement.
Keep the casualty's head, neck, and torso aligned in a straight line without bending or twisting.
Manually support the head in neutral position if trained and safe to do so.
Move an unconscious casualty ONLY if there is an imminent life hazard like vehicle fire, rising water, or oncoming unstopped traffic.
unsafe_actions: Do not shake, slap, or aggressively move an unconscious casualty.
Do not bend or twist the casualty's neck to place a pillow or cloth under their head.
Do not force an unconscious casualty into a sitting or standing position.
Do not attempt to administer liquids, water, or food into the mouth of an unconscious person.
escalation_criteria: Complete unresponsiveness to verbal or physical stimuli
Abnormal, gasping, or absent breathing
Visible head wounds, skull deformity, or bleeding from ears/nose
Loss of sensation, tingling, or paralysis in arms or legs reported prior to losing consciousness
Crash involved rollover, ejection from vehicle, or high-speed impact
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by Indian Red Cross First Aid Manual and WHO Trauma Care Protocols.

knowledge_records.topic: Emergency escalation after a road accident
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Under the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) instituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs, 112 is India's official single emergency number connecting callers to Police, Fire, Medical Ambulance (108/102), and Disaster Rescue. Escalation is required for any crash involving injury, vehicle fire, trapped occupants, fuel spills, highway blockages, or law-and-order threats.
safe_actions: Dial 112 immediately in India for pan-emergency dispatch (Police, Fire, Ambulance).
Call ambulance services (108 / 112) for physical trauma, unconsciousness, severe pain, or severe bleeding.
Call Fire & Rescue services (101 / 112) for active vehicle fires, smoke, fuel leaks, chemical spills, or trapped occupants requiring hydraulic cutting tools.
Call Police (100 / 112) to report fatal accidents, traffic obstructions, hit-and-run incidents, or public safety threats.
Stay online with the call taker and follow pre-arrival instructions.
unsafe_actions: Do not delay dialing 112 while attempting to manage a severe crash or fire independently.
Do not assume someone else has already called emergency services.
Do not leave the scene of a crash without reporting if you were involved in the collision.
escalation_criteria: Any casualty requiring medical attention
Unconsciousness, heavy bleeding, or breathing difficulty
Occupant pinned or trapped inside damaged vehicle structure
Presence of fire, smoke, fuel leakage, or hazardous material placards
Crash blocking high-speed highway traffic corridors
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by ERSS 112 Govt of India Guidelines and MoHFW National Health Portal.

knowledge_records.topic: What to communicate to emergency responders after a crash
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Clear call communication ensures appropriate responder dispatch. ERSS 112 and emergency medical protocols require providing the exact location/landmarks, number of vehicles, count and condition of casualties, and specific hazards (fire, fuel, electric, trapped occupants).
safe_actions: State clearly: 'There is a road traffic accident.'
Give the precise location: road name, highway milestone/kilometer stone, direction of travel (e.g., Jaipur to Delhi side), and prominent landmarks.
Specify the total number and types of vehicles involved (e.g., bus, truck, car, motorcycle, EV).
Report casualty details: total number of injured people, unconscious victims, heavy bleeding, or trapped occupants.
Report hazards: active fire, fuel leakage, electrical wire contact, or spilled cargo.
Provide your name and direct contact number for emergency callback.
unsafe_actions: Do not hang up until the emergency call taker explicitly instructs you to do so.
Do not guess location details; look for physical highway markers or map pins if unsure.
Do not exaggerate or minimize casualty numbers.
escalation_criteria: Any emergency call reporting a road crash in India
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by ERSS 112 Dispatch Standards and MoHFW Pre-Hospital Communication Protocols.

knowledge_records.topic: Highway, night, and low-visibility road accident safety
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: High-speed road corridors, night darkness, fog, and rain severely amplify secondary crash risk. NHAI and MoRTH highway codes mandate keeping all uninjured occupants behind steel crash barriers (metal beam crash barriers), deploying reflective warning triangles at a safe distance behind vehicles, turning on hazard lamps, and contacting highway patrol helplines (1033 on National Highways).
safe_actions: Immediately move all uninjured occupants over the shoulder barrier (behind safety guardrails) away from the road.
Activate hazard lights (all four blinkers) on all involved vehicles if operational.
On National Highways, dial 1033 (NHAI Toll-Free Helpline) or 112 for specialized highway patrol and ambulance response.
When visibility is low (fog/rain/night), use high-visibility clothing or phone flashlights aimed toward the ground (not into drivers' eyes) to remain visible.
Tell responders if the crash is located on a flyover, bridge, tunnel, or blind curve.
unsafe_actions: Do not allow occupants to sit inside a disabled vehicle parked on a high-speed highway shoulder or live lane.
Do not stand between two stopped vehicles on a highway shoulder.
Do not cross live highway lanes at night or during heavy fog.
Do not attempt roadside vehicle repairs in live carriageway lanes.
escalation_criteria: Crash on National Highway, Expressway, or fast arterial road
Nighttime, fog, dust storm, or torrential rain reducing visibility below 50 meters
Disabled vehicle stranded in live traffic lane or unlit road curve
Crash located on a bridge, flyover, or tunnel where no shoulder exists
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by NHAI Highway Safety Incident Protocols and MoRTH Traffic Safety Rules.

knowledge_records.topic: Accident-specific hazards: fire, fuel, smoke, electrical damage, and unstable vehicles
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Crash scenes containing active fires, fuel leaks, damaged high-voltage EV batteries, fallen power lines, or unstable overturned vehicles pose extreme hazards. NDMA and Fire Service protocols dictate keeping a minimum 50-meter safety perimeter, eliminating ignition sources, avoiding contact with high-voltage EV components, and escalating to specialized fire/rescue teams.
safe_actions: Maintain a minimum safety distance of 30-50 meters from vehicles leaking fuel, smoking, or burning.
Turn off the engine ignition of involved vehicles if safe to reach the keys without risk.
Keep all ignition sources, cigarettes, spark-producing tools, and open flames far away from liquid fuel spills.
Inform 112 / Fire services immediately if an Electric Vehicle (EV) is involved in a severe crash or exhibiting battery heating/hissing/smoke.
Stay clear of downed power cables or utility poles touching damaged vehicle frames.
unsafe_actions: Do not touch orange high-voltage cables, battery enclosures, or metal frames of a damaged Electric Vehicle.
Do not attempt to extinguish a massive engine or battery fire with water; use ABC dry powder fire extinguishers if trained and safe.
Do not enter or climb onto an unstable, overturned, or precariously balanced vehicle.
Do not inhale dense black smoke from burning vehicle interiors or tires.
escalation_criteria: Visible fire, sparks, or thick smoke coming from engine bay or underbody battery
Liquid fuel (petrol/diesel) leaking rapidly under or around vehicles
Electric Vehicle involved in high-impact collision with battery breach or thermal runaway signs
Power lines or electrical utility cables draped over crashed vehicles
Commercial tanker vehicle leaking liquid/gas cargo
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by NDMA Hazard Protocols and MHA Fire & Rescue Service Guidelines.

knowledge_records.topic: India-specific emergency contact and information to report
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: In India, the primary national unified emergency line is 112 (ERSS). Key service-specific numbers nationwide include 108 (Emergency Medical Ambulance Services operated across states), 100 (Police), 101 (Fire), and 1033 (NHAI National Highway Helpline). Callers must provide structured Indian location markers like landmarks, milestone numbers, or city toll plazas.
safe_actions: Dial 112 as the primary toll-free pan-India emergency number from any mobile or landline network (works even without active SIM/balance).
Dial 1033 specifically for crashes occurring on National Highways across India for dedicated NHAI patrol, ambulance, and tow recovery.
Dial 108 for state-operated emergency medical response ambulances.
Provide location using Indian road markers: National Highway number (e.g., NH-44), kilometer stone numbers, nearest toll plaza, or landmark (e.g., near petrol pump/dhaba).
Cooperate with local traffic police and ERSS call center dispatchers.
unsafe_actions: Do not use foreign emergency numbers (like 911 or 999) inside India.
Do not rely solely on state-specific local numbers when travelling across state borders on national highways; use 112 or 1033.
Do not cut the call before giving precise location landmarks.
escalation_criteria: Any road crash emergency occurring anywhere within Indian territory
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by ERSS 112 (MHA), MoRTH Road Safety Guidelines, and MoHFW National Health Portal.

knowledge_records.topic: Good Samaritan legal safety and protections in India
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Under MoRTH Gazette Notification S.O. 2508(E) and Supreme Court directives, a Good Samaritan (a bystander who voluntarily assists a road crash victim) is protected by law in India. Good Samaritans cannot be forced to reveal personal details, cannot be detained by police, cannot be forced to pay hospital registration fees, and are not required to give police testimony unless done voluntarily.
safe_actions: Know that assisting a road crash victim in India is protected under the Good Samaritan Law.
You can transport a crash victim to the nearest hospital without fear of police harassment or forced legal procedures.
You are NOT legally required to disclose your name, personal details, or phone number to hospital staff or police officers when admitting a victim.
Hospitals are legally prohibited from delaying treatment or demanding registration money from a Good Samaritan prior to attending to a trauma victim.
If you voluntarily choose to give police statement, it can be examined at a time and location of your convenience, including via video conferencing.
unsafe_actions: Do not hesitate or refrain from calling 112 or helping an injured crash victim due to fear of police or legal harassment.
Do not pay unauthorized hospital admission fees demanded for admitting an emergency crash victim.
Do not allow police officers to detain or compel you to stay at the hospital/police station unless you are an involved party/accused.
escalation_criteria: Bystander assisting crash victim faces harassment or forced detention from police or hospital staff
Hospital refuses emergency trauma admission to a road accident victim
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by MoRTH Gazette Notification S.O. 2508(E) and Supreme Court Good Samaritan Judgement.

knowledge_records.topic: What bystanders should avoid at a road accident scene
knowledge_records.evidence_summary: Bystander interference, gawking, crowding, and improper photo/video recording severely obstruct emergency services and cause secondary collisions. MoRTH road safety guidelines emphasize keeping carriageways clear, allowing emergency ambulance egress, and restricting bystander actions to safe assistance.
safe_actions: Keep roads and highway shoulders open for incoming ambulances and fire tenders.
Maintain a safe distance from active live lanes and crash debris.
Assist in directing passing traffic away from the crash scene if safe to do so from behind a barrier.
Clear out immediately once police, fire, or ambulance personnel arrive on scene.
unsafe_actions: Do not crowd around damaged vehicles or injured victims in active traffic lanes.
Do not stop your vehicle on live highway lanes to gawk, watch, or film videos of the accident.
Do not block approaching ambulance or fire rescue vehicles.
Do not touch or disturb physical crash evidence (weapons, vehicle parts, fluid trails) unless necessary to rescue a person.
escalation_criteria: Crowd is blocking emergency vehicle access or ambulance egress
Bystanders standing dangerously close to live high-speed traffic lanes
knowledge_records.notes: Backed by MoRTH Traffic Regulations and Indian Red Cross Bystander Guidelines.

human_review_required.conflict: 112 is pan-India integrated emergency, while 108 is state-managed ambulance dispatch. In some states, 112 seamlessly redirects to 108; in others, both run in parallel.
human_review_required.risk: Minimal - both numbers are official and free.
human_review_required.recommended_handling: Recommend 112 as primary unified line, with 108 specified for direct ambulance dispatch.

query_coverage.query: What should I do immediately after a road accident?
expected_answer_points: First protect yourself and assess scene safety for traffic, fire, or fuel hazards.
Move uninjured people away from live traffic if safe.
Call emergency services immediately at 112 (or 108 for ambulance).
Share exact location, vehicle count, casualty count, and hazards.

query_coverage.query: I witnessed a crash. How do I safely assess the scene?
expected_answer_points: Do not rush into moving traffic.
Look for fire, smoke, fuel smell, electrical hazards, or broken glass.
Approach only when it is safe without exposing yourself to traffic.
Dial 112 if hazards or casualties are present.

query_coverage.query: Should I move my car after an accident on a highway?
expected_answer_points: Move the vehicle to the hard shoulder only if drivable and safe.
If disabled in a live lane, turn on hazard lights immediately.
Get all occupants behind crash barriers and call 112 or 1033 (NHAI).

query_coverage.query: There is heavy traffic around the crash. Where should I stand?
expected_answer_points: Never stand in live traffic lanes or between stopped vehicles.
Move behind highway safety barriers or off the shoulder.
Keep all passengers off the carriageway.

query_coverage.query: The accident happened at night and visibility is poor. What should I do?
expected_answer_points: Turn on hazard warning lights immediately.
Move occupants off the road behind safety barriers.
Use phone flashlights directed toward the ground to stay visible.
Call 112 / 1033 and report low visibility.

query_coverage.query: When should emergency medical help be called after a crash?
expected_answer_points: Call 112 / 108 immediately for any injury, unconsciousness, heavy bleeding, chest impact, or trapped occupants.

query_coverage.query: What information should I tell emergency responders?
expected_answer_points: Exact location, road name, highway milestone, direction of travel.
Number and types of vehicles involved.
Number of casualties and severity (unconscious, trapped, heavy bleeding).
Hazards present (fire, fuel leak, EV battery, blocked lanes).

query_coverage.query: A person is unconscious after a road accident. What should a bystander do?
expected_answer_points: Call 112 / 108 immediately.
Check breathing from a safe position.
Keep the casualty's head and neck completely aligned and still.
Do not move them unless fire or direct danger is present.

query_coverage.query: Should I move someone who may have a neck or spinal injury?
expected_answer_points: Do NOT move the casualty unless there is an imminent life hazard like fire or oncoming traffic.
Keep head, neck, and torso strictly aligned.
Await trained medical ambulance staff.

query_coverage.query: There is heavy bleeding after the collision. What is the priority?
expected_answer_points: Call 112 / 108 immediately.
Apply firm, direct pressure on the bleeding wound with a clean cloth/pad.
Maintain direct pressure continuously until help arrives.
Do not remove embedded objects.

query_coverage.query: The vehicle is smoking. Is it safe to approach?
expected_answer_points: Maintain 30-50 meters distance; smoke indicates fire or thermal risk.
Call 112 / 101 immediately.
Warn others to stay clear.

query_coverage.query: What should I do if fuel is leaking from the crashed vehicle?
expected_answer_points: Stay clear of fuel spills and eliminate ignition sources (no smoking/sparks).
Dial 112 / 101 fire services immediately.
Keep bystanders at a safe perimeter.

query_coverage.query: What should I do if an electric vehicle is damaged in a crash?
expected_answer_points: Avoid touching orange high-voltage cables or battery enclosures.
Watch for battery hiss, heat, or smoke.
Call 112 and specify that an EV is involved.

query_coverage.query: Accident ke turant baad mujhe kya karna chahiye?
expected_answer_points: Apni aur scene ki safety check karein.
Hazards (traffic, fire, fuel leak) dekhein.
Uninjured logon ko road se door le jaayein.
112 par emergency call karein.

query_coverage.query: Road accident dekhne par scene ke paas kaise safely jaana chahiye?
expected_answer_points: Traffic mein mat bhaagein.
Fire, smoke, petrol smell aur electrical wires check karein.
Safe ho tabhi paas jaayein aur 112 call karein.

query_coverage.query: Highway par accident ho gaya hai, gaadi se bahar kahan khade hona chahiye?
expected_answer_points: Road barrier ke peeche safe shoulder par khade ho.
Live lane ya gaadi ke bilkul peeche mat khade ho.
Hazard lights turns on karein aur 1033 / 112 call karein.

query_coverage.query: घायल व्यक्ति को दुर्घटना के बाद कब नहीं हिलाना चाहिए?
expected_answer_points: रीढ़, गर्दन या सिर की चोट में घायल को न हिलाएं।
बेहोश व्यक्ति को बिना कारण न खींचें।
केवल आग या विस्फोट के खतरे में ही सुरक्षित स्थान पर ले जाएं।

query_coverage.query: सड़क दुर्घटना में पुलिस, एम्बुलेंस या फायर सर्विस को कब बुलाना चाहिए?
expected_answer_points: चोट या बेहोशी में 112 / 108 एम्बुलेंस बुलाएं।
आग, फ्यूल लीक या फंसे लोगों के लिए 112 / 101 फायर सर्विस बुलाएं।
नेशनल हाईवे पर 1033 पर भी कॉल कर सकते हैं।

query_coverage.query: क्या भारत में दुर्घटना पीड़ित की मदद करने वाले व्यक्ति को Good Samaritan सुरक्षा मिलती है?
expected_answer_points: Haan, MoRTH aur Supreme Court Good Samaritan law ke under full legal protection milti hai.
Police ya hospital aapko detain nahi kar sakti na personal details force kar sakti hai.
Hospital emergency victim ko admit karne se mana nahi kar sakta.

query_coverage.query: I am injured, the car is blocking a fast road, and another person is unconscious. What should be prioritized?
expected_answer_points: Ensure personal safety away from oncoming fast traffic.
Dial 112 immediately to report injury, road blockage, and unconscious person.
Do not move the unconscious person unless fire or incoming unstopped traffic poses an immediate death risk.

query_coverage.query: Can I switch on hazard lights and place a warning triangle after a highway crash?
expected_answer_points: Yes, turn on hazard warning lights immediately.
Place warning triangle behind vehicle only if you can do so safely without walking into live high-speed lanes.

query_coverage.query: There may be a damaged electrical system and fuel leak. What hazards should responders know about?
expected_answer_points: Report active fuel leaks or fuel smell.
Report electrical sparks, exposed wires, or EV involvement.
Report any trapped occupants.

query_coverage.query: Ambulance आने तक घायल व्यक्ति की मदद कैसे करें?
expected_answer_points: Victim ko quiet aur calm rakhein, unhe hilayein mat.
Heavy bleeding ho toh saaf kapde se direct pressure dein.
Pani ya khana mat dein.

query_coverage.query: What should a bystander avoid doing at a road accident scene?
expected_answer_points: Do not crowd or block emergency access.
Do not stand in live traffic to gawk or record videos.
Do not move casualties unnecessarily.
Do not touch fire, fuel, or high-voltage EV components.
